title: Dynamic Programming
summary: 1D and 2D tables, LIS, LCS, edit distance, knapsack

guide.title: Stop solving the same thing twice
points: Dynamic programming (DP) turns exponential brute force into polynomial time by remembering answers to smaller problems.
It is the topic that separates candidates in product-company rounds: knapsack, LIS, edit distance and coin change are classics.
Once you see the pattern ("best way to reach state X"), many hard-looking questions become a table to fill.

guide.title: DP in products you use
points: Spell check and "did you mean" use edit distance between words; git diff uses longest common subsequence.
Maps and ride apps compute shortest routes with DP-style relaxation (Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall).
Budget planners and cargo loading are knapsack problems: the most value within a weight or cost limit.
Text justification in word processors and speech recognition (Viterbi) are DP too.

guide.title: State, choice, base case
points: State: what you need to know to describe a sub-problem, e.g. dp[i] = best answer for the first i items.
Transition: how dp[i] is built from smaller states, e.g. dp[i] = max(dp[i − 1], dp[i − 2] + a[i]).
Base case: the answer for the smallest states (dp[0], dp[1]).
Beginner route: write the recursion first, add memoisation, then turn it into a loop (tabulation).

guide.title: Climbing stairs: memo and table
points: Ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps: ways(n) = ways(n − 1) + ways(n − 2).

guide.title: 1-D DP: take it or leave it
points: House robber: at each house either skip it (dp[i − 1]) or rob it and skip the previous (dp[i − 2] + a[i]).
Coin change: dp[x] = fewest coins for amount x = 1 + min over coins c of dp[x − c].
Only the last two values are needed? Keep two variables instead of an array: O(1) memory.

code.python:
prev, cur = 0, 0
for x in houses:
    prev, cur = cur, max(cur, prev + x)
return cur

guide.title: 2-D DP: two strings or items × capacity
points: Longest common subsequence: dp[i][j] for the first i characters of a and the first j of b. Equal characters extend the diagonal; otherwise take the better of dropping one.
0/1 knapsack: dp[w] = best value within weight w. Loop the weight backwards so each item is used once.

guide.title: States × choices
points: Time = number of states × work per state. LCS has n·m states and O(1) work: O(n·m).
Memory can often drop one dimension: keep only the previous row.
Spot DP: "count the ways", "minimum / maximum cost", "is it possible", with choices that overlap.

guide.title: What breaks DP code
points: A state that misses information (e.g. ignoring whether the last item was taken).
Wrong base case: dp[0] = 1 for counting ways, but 0 for "minimum coins".
Wrong loop order: a state is read before it is filled. In 0/1 knapsack a forward loop reuses an item.
Unreachable states left as 0 instead of Infinity / −1 in "minimum" problems.

guide.title: For advanced learners and interviews
points: Explain in this order: state, transition, base case, answer, complexity. Interviewers grade exactly that.
LIS in O(n log n) with patience sorting (binary search over tails).
Other families: interval DP (matrix chain, burst balloons), DP on trees, bitmask DP over subsets, digit DP.
Rebuild the actual choice (not just the value) by walking back through the table.
Next step: Maths and Bits.

problems.title: Climbing stairs
problems.statement: You climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of ways to climb n steps (1 <= n <= 40).

problems.title: House robber
problems.statement: You cannot take from two neighbouring houses. Return the largest total you can take.
inputFormat: money: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: At each house: best without it, or best two back plus this one.

problems.title: Fewest coins
problems.statement: You have unlimited coins of the given values. Return the fewest coins that make the amount, or -1.
inputFormat: coins: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)

problems.title: Unique grid paths
problems.statement: Moving only right or down, return the number of paths from the top-left to the bottom-right cell.
problems.hint: Each cell is the sum of the cell above and the cell to the left.

problems.title: Longest increasing subsequence
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
inputFormat: nums: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: dp[i] = 1 + best dp[j] with nums[j] < nums[i]; or keep smallest tails and binary search.

problems.title: Longest common subsequence
problems.statement: Return the length of the longest subsequence common to both strings.
problems.hint: Match: diagonal + 1. Otherwise: max of up and left.

problems.title: 0/1 knapsack
problems.statement: Each item can be taken at most once. Return the largest total value with total weight within capacity.
inputFormat: weights: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
values: integers separated by spaces (may be empty)
problems.hint: dp[c] = max(dp[c], dp[c - w] + v), with c going down.

problems.title: Edit distance
problems.statement: Return the fewest single-character insertions, deletions or replacements that turn a into b.
problems.hint: Same table as LCS, with three neighbours.
